title: Win direct routes and add seats on full routes

blocks.text: The first supply theme covers how visitors reach the province and move through it. It holds three focus areas: air access, cruise and internal mobility. The December entry on visa and safety deficits left this theme for section 3.3.2.
Theme 2.1 · Accessibility, connectivity and infrastructure · Focus area 7
Win direct routes and add seats on full routes
Eleven of 27 international routes run above 80% load and carriers raise fares before seats, so the province must win frequency and larger aircraft now, ahead of runway relief in about 2033.
**December 2025.** Close the Air Access and Cruise Capacity Gaps (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64). The air half of the entry became this focus area and the cruise half became focus area 8.

**October 2026: Reworded.** The reason is full routes and fares before seats: eleven routes run above 80% load and sixteen at 75% or more (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "Seasonality"). MIDAS and the Infrastructure Report's air-access section drove the change.

blocks.message: The network is full on its best routes, the airport is full at its runway at peak, and planned relief lands after the base case crosses the model's seat line.

blocks.text: The Infrastructure Report puts the timing problem in one line: the certain fix is the latest, and the earliest big-capacity option is the least certain (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p109). No airline took part in the first phase of stakeholder engagement, so the carriers' own view of frequency and gauge is still to be tested (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p16).

Wesgro should split the air agenda by horizon. Until about 2032 the job is to fill and enlarge what already flies: frequency and larger aircraft on the full routes, hub-carrier capacity and the five regional routes MIDAS names. After that, the job is to have direct India and China route cases ready when runway capacity arrives. The Demand-Side Analysis lists the moves: added frequency from Emirates, Qatar Airways and Ethiopian Airlines, long-term route cases for India and China and coordinated airline incentives through Cape Town Air Access (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p54).

rows: Run a seat-retention and frequency programme on the full routes, with joint marketing tied to route performance
Scale and ring-fence Cape Town Air Access's route fund as a public-private fund for route support, with a set size and governance
Air Access; DEDAT; City of Cape Town; private sector

Escalate bilateral air service agreements, the cap on US carriers and immigration processing at Cape Town International

blocks.text: Chile treated its gateway airport as economic infrastructure: a private concession funded a ~US$900 million expansion at Santiago, and international seats grew ~40% to 50% between 2013 and 2019 under open-skies agreements (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p23, p25, p26). For the Western Cape the lesson splits by tier. The province can scale its existing route fund; open skies and private airport finance are national levers, so this report carries them in the escalation agenda (focus area 19). Chile's 2024 surge also came mostly overland: land borders carried 55.6% of arrivals and Argentina about 40% (Sernatur, Anuario de Turismo 2024, Dec 2025).

**Initiative I6**, route development and seat retention with a public-private air access fund (section 4.3). **Indicators** T1-01 international arrivals at impact level, and T2-09 seats and routes and T2-10 seats added on full routes at outcome level (section 5.2).
